title: NetBench — TCP vs UDP Network Performance
description: Real TCP/UDP application-level socket performance exported via OpenTelemetry and queried from Prometheus. TCP packet loss and packet counts are not measured. Cumulative stat means and rolling chart means are not latest-test gauges; loopback is not physical network performance.

panels.title: Total Successful Tests
panels.description: Cumulative observations since the current Flask SDK process started, not the latest test and not a total limited to the selected dashboard time range. Compare contributes one TCP and one UDP test.

panels.title: Successful Tests by Protocol
panels.description: Cumulative observations since the current Flask SDK process started, not the latest test and not a total limited to the selected dashboard time range.

options.content:
TCP **green** · UDP **purple**.

Stats: cumulative since SDK startup. Charts: rolling observations.

**TCP packet statistics unavailable.** UDP loss: DATA sequences. Localhost: loopback. Application RTT: not ICMP.

panels.title: Average Throughput
panels.description: Cumulative observations since the current Flask SDK process started, not the latest test and not a total limited to the selected dashboard time range. Mean Mbps; UDP is receiver goodput.

panels.title: Average Application RTT
panels.description: Cumulative observations since the current Flask SDK process started, not the latest test and not a total limited to the selected dashboard time range. Application request/response including peer processing; not ICMP ping.

panels.title: Throughput over Time
panels.description: Rolling per-test mean from histogram increases over $__rate_interval (at least 2 minutes). Gaps mean no new observations in the window, not zero performance. SDK exports every 30 seconds; values are not instantaneous link speed.

panels.title: Application RTT over Time
panels.description: Rolling per-test mean from histogram increases over $__rate_interval (at least 2 minutes). Gaps mean no new observations in the window, not zero performance. SDK exports every 30 seconds; values are not instantaneous link speed. Application RTT, not ICMP.

panels.title: Average Transfer Duration
panels.description: Cumulative observations since the current Flask SDK process started, not the latest test and not a total limited to the selected dashboard time range. TCP includes final ACK; UDP includes 150 ms reorder window and control exchange/retries. Durations have different semantics.

panels.title: Payload Bytes Sent & Received
panels.description: Cumulative observations since the current Flask SDK process started, not the latest test and not a total limited to the selected dashboard time range. Payload bytes only. TCP received count is validated by final ACK; UDP received bytes are unique DATA payloads.

panels.title: Average UDP Packet Loss
panels.description: Cumulative observations since the current Flask SDK process started, not the latest test and not a total limited to the selected dashboard time range. Arithmetic mean of per-test loss percentages, not packet-weighted loss. TCP unavailable.

panels.title: UDP DATA Packets
panels.description: Cumulative observations since the current Flask SDK process started, not the latest test and not a total limited to the selected dashboard time range. Received counts unique sequence numbers. No TCP packet statistics.

panels.title: UDP Packet Loss over Time
panels.description: Rolling per-test mean from histogram increases over $__rate_interval (at least 2 minutes). Gaps mean no new observations in the window, not zero performance. SDK exports every 30 seconds; values are not instantaneous link speed. UDP-only mean per-test percentage, not a TCP loss estimate.

panels.title: Successful Test Activity over Time
panels.description: Estimated successful test increases per rolling $__rate_interval window. Prometheus extrapolation can produce fractional counts. Resets are handled by increase; the first sample alone cannot establish an increase.
